title: First trip to Chicago with Manuel Perez
summary: Picou went to Chicago before World War I with Manuel Perez, working at Johnson's Cabaret and a State Street theatre.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Yeah, with Papa Celestein, no? Yes, you travelled to the T.O.M.C.E. Papa Celestein. When you first went to Chicago, what band was that, when you first went to Chicago, who did you play with? Oh, I played with Manuel Perez. Manuel Perez. Yeah. Do you remember where that was and about when? Do you remember? Oh, I remember it was at Johnson's Cabaret, and the theatre. Oh, what's the name of the theatre? I was playing with the best piano player out there. What's the name of the theatre? There was a monogram or the grand theatre. Grand theatre. Grand theatre. Grand theatre. On State Street. Yes, on State Street. That's right, 27. When did you go? Was it during the war, before that first world war? Oh, before. Before. Before the war. Before the war.
Do you remember who was in the band? Mm-hm.

Mm-hm. Charlie Booker. And they said he was getting sort of rusty and a little old. He couldn't finger like he used to. And the leader said, oh, we can't use him. So Manuel said, I'll tell you who to get. This man, as long as he lives, he'll play as well as he ever did. He said, you send for Mr. Peek Coot. That's it. That's it. That's it. You said the right thing. Yeah, Manuel said, as long as that man lives, he's going to play. Send for me. That's what he said. Yes, indeed. You're right. You're right. Pete Coot can play. Yes, indeed. I guess McCurdy wasn't doing so well in those days. Oh. They didn't want him when they came out. Well, blow something for me. Oh, I can't play at all, Alphonse. I've only had just a few lessons. He's only been taking lessons about one month is all. Oh, you're very good.
